To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have synthesized new α-mangostins derivatives with Mannich base fragments and have demonstrated that they are more efficient than α-mangostine in protecting erythrocyte membranes from H2O2 damage.
the Mannich reaction of 4-oxo derivative of α-mangostatins with formaldehyde and morpholine and piperidine amines leads to the formation of novel compounds with high membrane-protective properties.
α-Mangostin and its C-4-alkylation derivatives have been synthesized; the Mannich reaction was used to obtain α-mangostins with a morpholinomethyl or piperidinylmethyl fragment at the C-1′ position.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for new derivatives of α-magnostin with high biological activity.
the synthesis and biological activity of a number of α-mangosin derivatives.

the development of novel derivatives of the natural xanthone α-mangostins with enhanced antioxidant activity and membrane-protecting effect, and with the study of the structure-activity relationship for this class of compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
α-mangostins are a class of compounds with high potential for further research in order to develop novel drugs for the prevention and treatment of oxidative stress-related diseases.
the Mannich base of α-mangostatine with a morpholinomethyl fragment is a new promising compound with a high membrane-protective and antioxidant activity.
the C-4-alkylated and C-4-arylated derivatives of α-mongostin possess the membrane-protective properties and may be used as the basis for the creation of new biologically active substances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of the morpholinomethyl group into α-mangostins is the key for obtaining new derivatives with improved biological activity.
the Mannich base of α-mangosten containing morpholinomethy group at C-4 is the most promising compound for further studies of its biological properties.
the Mannich reaction is a promising tool for obtaining new derivatives of α-magnostin with enhanced biological activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mannich base of α-mangostenin with piperidine fragment is a promising candidate for further development as a drug for the treatment of inflammatory diseases.
α-mangostins with the C-4-alkylated phenolic fragment can have high antioxidant activity.

the Mannich reaction can be used for the synthesis of α-mangostenin derivatives with a wide range of antioxidant and membrane-protector activity, which is of great importance for their use as biologically active compounds in the development of drugs.
